primitives.name: Healthy-Worker Survivor Effect Correction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research question Does recent playing load causally increase injury hazard in the NBA, or does the naive association (heavy recent minutes look *protective*) merely reflect the healthy-worker survivor effect — injured/fragile players getting rested, so that only durable players accumulate load?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{HR}_{\\text{naive}}': 'naive hazard ratio (dimensionless)', '\\text{HR}_{\\text{corrected}}': 'causal hazard ratio (dimensionless)', '\\gamma': 'naive regression coefficient (dimensionless)', '\\beta': 'causal regression coefficient (dimensionless)', '\\text{load}': 'player load (minutes)'}
primitives.assumptions: Injured players are more likely to be rested, leading to selection bias in observed load distributions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When injury reporting is incomplete or delayed relative to load accumulation.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that in observational settings where players self-select into high-load scenarios, naive associations between load and injury are biased due to the healthy-worker survivor effect. Players who sustain injuries are often removed from high-load situations, skewing the distribution of load among survivors. The MS-PEM framework addresses this by constructing a marginal structural model that adjusts for selection bias using inverse probability weights derived from a propensity model. These weights stabilize the influence of observed covariates on treatment assignment, allowing estimation of the counterfactual hazard of injury under hypothetical load trajectories. The piecewise exponential model allows flexible modeling of time-varying hazards, while the spline-based WCE encodes temporal dependencies in load history. The key mathematical duality lies between the observed association (which may be spurious) and the causal effect (which requires adjustment). Failure modes include unmeasured confounding such as latent fitness, which violates conditional exchangeability. The model’s validity hinges on strong assumptions about positivity and consistency, and its robustness depends on accurate specification of the propensity model and appropriate truncation of weights.
